title: Acting and Reacting in Different Situations (1)

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You are visiting the park and see a bottle on the ground next to the rubbish bin. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: You are not responsible for other people, but lending a helping hand and caring is often the right thing to do.

atoms.text: You pick the bottle up and throw it away in the next rubbish or recycling bin.
You ignore the bottle — at least you didn’t throw it there.
You throw your own bottle next to it.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You are working on a science project and don’t know what to do next. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: When you run into problems, it’s always best to try to figure it out yourself first. Try to be patient with yourself; most people don’t get things on their first try! If, after you’ve already tried to understand it yourself, you still don’t get it, then it is time to ask for help.

atoms.text: You try to figure it out first. You reread your science book, look at your notes and don’t get frustrated if it takes a while.
You ask a friend if they know what to do next and if they can help you.
You immediately get frustrated, give up and go outside to play instead.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You are beginning to feel overwhelmed. It’s the end of term, you have a lot of homework due and you don’t know where to start.

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: When you are overwhelmed, sometimes the best thing to do is make a plan. Doing everything at once makes it seem like there’s not enough time for anything. When you have a plan, you can see that it might be challenging, but that you will be able to accomplish your goals.

atoms.text: Get organised. Make a calendar of when everything is due and when you have time. Schedule the days and times when you will work on different topics.
Work every day after school without a plan and just try to get everything done as quickly as possible.
Ignore the work. Don’t tell your parents or teacher it feels like too much and wait for it to go away.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You are very excited about your new, complex game. It needs to be set up and built from pieces in the box. You really want to play right now. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: Here, if you unwrap everything without knowing what to do, you risk losing pieces and missing important information that would help you put it together. It can feel hard when you’re very excited, but being patient can save you time and headaches.

atoms.text: Carefully read the instructions before getting all the small pieces out. Only unpack things when you know what to do with them.
atoms.sound: Carefully reed the instructions before getting all the small pieces out. Only unpack things when you know what to do with them.

atoms.text: Take things out of the box and unwrap them while reading the instructions as you go.
Hurriedly take out all the pieces and unwrap them as fast as possible.
